rubric_name: Gemini style / quality / hygiene guide codebase evaluation rubric
source_limitations: The earlier Code Quality shell capture has been superseded by Code Quality_ An Exhaustive Breakdown - Google Gemini (2).mht.

rules.basis: Intention-revealing names; avoid cryptic identifiers and generic implementation names where domain names exist.
Spatial rhythm, formatting, bounded line length, bounded function length, and shallow indentation keep code readable at 3 AM.
Comments explain why/global state/intent, not compensate for unclear how.
Hardcoded strings/numbers should generally be named constants/enums unless local and obvious.
Functions should generally be single-purpose and often split above 20–30 lines if cohesion is mixed.
Avoid unnecessary repeated work, especially inside loops; prefer cached/indexed forms for repeated lookups.
Use explicit error handling; no bare except, silent pass, or Pokemon catching without diagnostics.
Treat external input as malicious; sanitize, validate, and avoid hardcoded credentials/secrets.
Critical paths and complex logic should have descriptive tests, ideally with Arrange-Act-Assert shape.
Code should be environment-agnostic and avoid local machine assumptions.
A reader should follow the narrative arc of data without hidden side effects or teleporting state.
Avoid mixing broad refactors with unrelated behavior changes; preserve atomic known-good states.
Avoid needless abstractions, over-generic internals, interface sprawl, and speculative architecture.
Domain values should cross boundaries through typed request/result/value objects rather than raw dict/object/stringly blobs.
Avoid deep nested control flow; use guard clauses to keep happy path visible.
Avoid mutable public representation leakage and public globals that downstream code can mutate.
Rust unsafe must be fenced and documented; unwrap/expect/panic/todo are unacceptable in production paths; sync mutex must not cross await.
Dependencies and external tools should be explicit, minimal, and audit-gated.
